name: Surveyor 1 lander

location.name: Oceanus Procellarum (Ocean of Storms), north of the crater Flamsteed

headline: America's first soft landing on the Moon, and 11,240 pictures of where it stood
story: At 06:17 UT on 2 June 1966, Surveyor 1 settled onto a flat plain in the southwest of the Ocean of Storms, inside an old crater about 100 kilometers wide, north of Flamsteed. It touched down at about 3 meters per second. On the first try, NASA had landed a spacecraft gently on the Moon.

Its camera began sending pictures at once. By nightfall on 14 June it had returned 10,338 of them, showing a surface firm enough to hold a lander. Then it survived the two-week lunar night and took more photographs on its second lunar day, for 11,240 in all.

Its battery voltage dropped sharply after sunset, and the mission ended on 13 July 1966. Engineers kept calling it until 7 January 1967. Decades later, NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter photographed Surveyor 1 from orbit, still standing on the plain where it landed.

facts.label: First
facts.value: U.S. soft landing on the Moon
